t: I heard the first cry and knew {god} had stayed with us.
The room went quiet, then the child cried. I thanked {god} at once.
I watched the mother hold on until {god} brought the child through.
Both were breathing when it ended. {god} was merciful in that room.
The child came safely after a hard labor. I saw an answered prayer.
I stood near the door and prayed until I heard the child.
The healer worked, the mother endured, and {god} brought them through.
I saw the child open their eyes. That was {god}'s kindness.
The birth turned dangerous, but {god} did not abandon them.
I watched a new life enter this village under {god}'s protection.
The mother asked for {god}, and the child arrived safely soon after.
Nobody in that room stood alone. {god} was with every one of us.
I heard the child cry and wanted to call it a blessing.
Both survived. I thanked the healer first and {god} quietly afterward.
The labor was hard, then suddenly it was over. Maybe somebody listened.
I prayed near the door, though I cannot say what helped.
The child was quiet at first. When they cried, everyone breathed again.
I saw skilled hands and good fortune. There may have been more.
The mother held on longer than I thought anyone could.
A safe birth makes me wonder whether my doubts are too easy.
The room felt different when the child arrived. I cannot explain that.
I expected the worst and watched both of them survive.
Perhaps {god} helped. I know the people beside her certainly did.
I left that room more grateful than certain.
I watched the healer work until the child was safely born.
The mother did the hardest work in that room. Remember that part.
I heard prayers, but I saw people save that birth.
The child cried because their lungs worked. That was enough for me.
It was a difficult birth with a good ending, not a mystery.
Everyone credits {god} after forgetting who cleaned the blood.
I stood in the room. Nothing happened without human hands.
The healer knew what to do, and the mother was strong.
A safe birth is wonderful without being divine.
I watched skilled work succeed. Calling it a miracle hides the lesson.
The child came late and healthy. Births do that sometimes.
I am glad they survived. Gratitude does not require a god.
They say the birth was difficult, but {god} guarded both lives.
Word came that the child cried strongly. {god} was kind.
I heard the mother's prayer was answered before dawn.
They say both are safe. Maybe prayer helped; good hands certainly did.
I heard the child came safely after a long night.
The story sounds like luck until people mention how close it came.
The healer delivered the child safely. People have added {god} since.
I heard mother and child are well. That is the whole useful story.
People call it divine because they were frightened first.
I saw the bolt choose one person beneath an empty sky.
{god} struck them before anyone could move. I will remember that warning.
I watched judgment fall without thunder or rain.
One moment they stood there, and the next {god} had answered.
The clear sky made {god}'s intent impossible to miss.
I saw {god}'s power land on a person. Nobody nearby spoke afterward.
Lightning struck them from a clear sky. I still do not know why.
I saw the bolt land, and belief became harder to avoid.
Maybe it was judgment. That possibility bothers me more than chance.
The person fell before I heard anything. I cannot call that ordinary.
I watched it happen and still cannot decide whether {god} meant it.
There were no clouds. That leaves me with questions I dislike.
I saw lightning strike a person. Strange weather is still weather.
The sky was clear, but clear skies do not prove intent.
A person died, and everyone immediately invented a reason.
I witnessed a terrible accident. I did not witness judgment.
The bolt was real. The meaning came from frightened people afterward.
I saw the person fall. Nobody can honestly say why it happened.
I watched new growth cover the bare ground after {god} acted.
The plants thickened before us. {god} had answered our need.
I saw the field fill out in moments. That was providence.
{god} made poor ground generous while we watched.
Fresh shoots rose where there had been almost nothing.
I watched {god} give the village another harvest.
The field changed while I stood there. Maybe we were helped.
I saw new growth appear too quickly for any season I know.
The plants rose together. I have no ordinary answer for that.
I wanted food, and the ground changed. I am still considering that.
It looked like a blessing. I am not ready to swear it was.
The growth was real. Whether it was an answer remains harder.
I saw the field improve quickly. We may have missed earlier growth.
Plants grow unevenly. People notice only when the change suits a story.
The ground was better than we thought. That happens without a god.
I watched the plants, not the sky. The plants had enough water.
A good patch became a better patch. Fear made it seem sudden.
The field changed, but calling every change divine teaches us nothing.
{god} threw {whom} so hard that nobody dared approach at first.
I watched {whom} leave the ground under {god}'s hand.
{whom} crossed half the square without taking a step. {god} did that.
I ran toward {whom} only after {god} released them.
{god} lifted {whom} from their feet and cast them aside.
I saw {whom} fly. No human hand was near them.
{whom} landed hard, and I thanked {god} they still moved.
Nobody touched {whom}. {god}'s warning was plain enough.
I saw {whom} rise, but I looked away before they landed.
{whom} flew past me. I still cannot say what moved them.
I ran when {whom} left the ground. Courage returned afterward.
Nobody was near {whom}. I wish that made the answer simpler.
I checked on {whom} after they landed. They could barely speak.
{whom} went up suddenly. I did not see where they came down.
I saw the throw clearly. Its meaning is what I cannot settle.
Something sent {whom} across the ground. I am not naming it yet.
{whom} stumbled before they flew. People leave that part out.
I saw {whom} fall hard. I did not measure the distance.
Everyone ran from {whom}, which made the throw look worse.
{whom} was hurt, but frightened witnesses have stretched the story.
I checked where {whom} landed. The marks were real; the explanation was not.
Nobody touched {whom}, but that does not prove a god did.
I saw {whom} leave the ground. I also saw confusion everywhere.
{whom} landed nearby. The tale already sends them twice as far.
{god} protected that birth. I am glad you told me.
A safe child deserves thanks at the shrine.
That sounds like mercy arriving through capable hands.
Maybe {god} helped. Either way, I am relieved.
I can believe the birth was fortunate without knowing why.
That is the kind of story that makes doubt less comfortable.
Credit the mother and healer before anybody invisible.
A good birth is good news. It is not evidence.
I am pleased they survived. Leave the explanation there.
{god} made that field answer our hunger.
We asked for abundance, and abundance came.
Gather all of it. Gifts should not be wasted.
Maybe it was help. We should use it before debating it.
That growth is difficult to explain and easy to welcome.
I am not certain it was divine, but I noticed.
Healthy soil needs no blessing to do its work.
People always discover providence after counting a good yield.
Harvest first. Invent meanings after the stores are full.
{god} judged them openly. We should pay attention.
That clear sky makes the warning plain.
Power like that should make everyone examine their conduct.
I believe the strike happened. I fear believing it was deserved.
That sounds deliberate, though I wish it did not.
If {god} chose them, I need to understand the reason.
A strange bolt does not become justice because people fear it.
Nobody knows what the dead person deserved. Stop pretending.
You saw lightning. The judgment was added afterward.
